q: 1. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD software uses vector analysis to transform and project 3D object coordinates into a 2D perspective view.

q: 2. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of product including civil construction, are known as
explain: Working drawings provide all necessary dimensions and details required to actually manufacture or build the project.

q: 3. The points at which the curve of intersection changes its nature are known as .............
explain: The points on an interpenetration curve where its geometric nature changes (e.g., where the curve crosses from one surface generator to another) are termed intersection points in this context.

q: 4. "Perspective Drawing" is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image .......
options: as it is drawn on a computer
as it is felt by the hands
as it is perceived by the eye
explain: Perspective drawing aims to represent an object on a flat surface the way it is actually perceived by the human eye.

q: 5. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and plane of projection are
explain: The word 'ortho' means right angle; the projectors (lines of sight) must be perpendicular to the projection plane.

q: 6. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off
explain: In a full section, the cutting plane passes entirely through the object, effectively removing one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 7. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: Sectional views allow designers to show internal holes, cavities, and assembly details that are hidden from the outside.

q: 8. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called
explain: Perspective drawing is the only projection method that accurately replicates the human visual experience.

q: 9. The point in space where parallel lines meet are called
explain: In perspective, all parallel lines that are not parallel to the picture plane appear to converge at a 'Vanishing Point'.

q: 10. Natural view of the object is represented by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is the marked correct answer; conventionally a perspective (prospective) projection is what represents the natural, real-life appearance of an object, but the key selects 'none of these' here.

q: 11. The system of orthographic projection is classified according to the relationship formed between
explain: First angle and third angle projection are classified based on the relative arrangement of the observer, the object and the projection plane.

q: 12. One method of preparing perspective of an object is
explain: The 'Vanishing Point Method' (or Office Method) is a standard geometric technique used to construct perspective views.

q: 13. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: The complete orthographic system generally uses six principal views.

q: 14. Plan, elevation and sections are
explain: Plans, elevations and sections are all views obtained by orthographic (parallel, perpendicular) projection.

q: 15. The locus of centre of curvature is known as
explain: In mathematics and geometry, the 'evolute' of a curve is the locus of all its centers of curvature.

q: 16. The isometric view of a sphere is
explain: A sphere looks identical from any viewing direction, so its isometric projection remains a true circle, unlike other solids.

q: 17. Number of faces in a dodecahedron are .............
explain: A dodecahedron is a regular polyhedron with 12 pentagonal faces, as reflected in its name ('dodeca' = twelve).

q: 18. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in
explain: First Angle Projection places the object in the 1st Quadrant (between the observer and the plane).

q: 19. If three orthographic views of a sphere containing a circular hole are drawn, the maximum number of circles that may appear altogether .............
explain: In three orthographic views (front, top, side) of a sphere with a hole, each view can show up to two circles (the sphere's outline and the hole), and with some overlap/coincidence considerations, the maximum count altogether works out to 4 as per this reference.

q: 20. An orthographic view of a hemisphere may appear as .............
explain: Viewed from directly above (or below) along its axis, a hemisphere's orthographic projection appears as a circle (the boundary of its flat circular face or the outline of the curved surface).

q: 21. Section lining is drawn with line at
explain: By convention, hatching/section lines are drawn at 45 degrees to the main outline of the sectioned part.

q: 22. The principal of oblique view drawing is to keep:
options: width and height axes at 90 degree
width, height and depth axes at 90 degree
explain: In Oblique projection, the front face (width and height) is kept parallel to the plane and at $90^{\circ}$ to each other, showing its true shape.

q: 23. Which of the following would be considered a primitive in a 3D solid modeling system?
explain: In 3D solid modeling, basic 3D shapes like the cylinder (along with cube, sphere, cone) are called primitives, forming the building blocks for constructing complex solids; square, rhombus, and spline are 2D/curve entities, not 3D primitives.

q: 24. Orthographic projection means .............
explain: 'Orthographic' derives from the Greek for 'right/straight writing,' referring to projection at a right angle (90°) — projectors perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 25. In the first angle projection
options: The plan is above the front view
The plan is directly below the front view
The plan is as in the third angle projection
explain: In first angle projection the plan (top view) is placed below the front view, opposite to the third angle convention.

q: 26. Which one is not engineerirg drawing?
explain: Cinema slides are artistic/entertainment media, not technical engineering drawings like building plans, road sections or machine elevations.

q: 27. *In isometric view a circle is seen as :
explain: Due to the 30-degree tilt in isometric projection, circles on the principal planes always appear as ellipses.

q: 28. *In orthographic projection, the projection's are always ........... to the plane of projection
explain: Orthographic projection is a system where the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 29. To emphasize the features on the side of an object the receding lines are drawn at the following angle to the plane of projection .............
explain: Drawing receding lines at an angle less than 45° reduces distortion on the side faces and helps emphasize/showcase the features on the side of the object in oblique projection.

q: 30. In oblique projections, a semi circle parallel to the plane of projection appears as .............
explain: Any plane figure that is parallel to the plane of projection in oblique projection is not foreshortened and hence retains its true shape — so a semicircle parallel to the plane still appears as a semicircle.

q: 31. The projectors in oblique projections are .............
explain: In oblique projection, the parallel projectors strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., they are inclined to the plane of projection (unlike orthographic projection where they are perpendicular).

q: 32. In the cavalier projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cavalier projection is characterized by receding lines drawn to full (true) scale with projectors typically inclined at 45° in most texts, but per this reference the projector angle is taken as 63°26'.

q: 33. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is a:
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane is viewed 'end-on' from that plane, so its projection collapses to a single point.

q: 34. Presentation drawing are generally rendered due to
explain: Rendering in presentation drawings adds shadows, textures, and lighting to create a realistic effect for the viewer.

q: 35. The type of pictorial projection generally used by the architects is .............
explain: Architects commonly use perspective projection to present realistic, client-friendly visualizations of how a finished building will actually appear to an observer.

q: 36. Horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP) are always
explain: In the standard system of orthographic projection, HP and VP are set up perpendicular to each other, intersecting along the reference line (XY line).

q: 38. If the top view of a plane is a rhombus the object may be .............
explain: A rhombus-shaped top view can result from either a true rhombus lying flat, or a square viewed while inclined to the plane of projection (its edges foreshortening unevenly), so the object may be either a square or a rhombus.

q: 39. The trace of a hexagonal plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an equilateral triangle' is marked as the answer for this item, reflecting a specific inclined orientation of the hexagonal plane considered in this reference.

q: 40. The projection obtained on a plane when the projectors converge to a point is known as
explain: Perspective projection uses projectors that converge at a single station point (the observer's eye), unlike parallel-projector methods.

q: 41. The length of the rectangle representing the development of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder is equal to :
options: twice the circumference of circular base
explain: When a cylinder is 'unrolled,' the length of the resulting rectangle is the distance around the circle, which is the circumference ($2\pi r$).

q: 42. If both the principle views of a plane object are ellipse of the same size, the side view will be .............
explain: When both front and top views appear as equal-sized ellipses, the plane is inclined to both HP and VP; consequently its side view (edge view) appears as an inclined straight line.

q: 43. Third angle projection is the traditional ........... system.
explain: Third-angle projection is primarily used in the United States and Canada, whereas Europe and Asia typically use First-angle.

q: 44. Among the following solids, a regular polyhedron is .............
explain: A regular polyhedron has all faces as identical regular polygons meeting in the same way at each vertex; among the given options, only the cube (all faces equal squares) satisfies this, while a sphere is not a polyhedron at all.

q: 45. The projection in which the length, breadth and height of an object is shown in one view is Known as :
explain: Isometric projection is a type of pictorial projection that shows all three dimensions in a single view at specific angles.

q: 46. The shades and shadows are :
options: the result of object on the ground
the result of light on the ground
explain: Shades refer to the dark parts on the object itself, while shadows are the dark areas cast by the object onto another surface.

q: 47. The face of an object containing circles, irregular shapes, etc. is kept parallel to the plane of projection is known as .............
explain: In oblique projection, the face with circular or irregular details is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it can be drawn true to shape without distortion, while other faces recede at an angle.

q: 48. The base angles used for drawing an isometric projection are:
explain: Isometric drawing uses one vertical (0° from vertical) axis and two receding axes drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 49. The curve of intersection of a vertical cone with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting a cone parallel to one of its generators (slant lines) produces a parabolic section, as per the conic section relationships.

q: 50. Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections :
options: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
the object must the situated in the first quadrant
the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
projections are obtained by drawing perpendicular s from the object to the planes
explain: While the planes are assumed transparent in 3rd angle, the statement is contextually marked incorrect based on general principle definitions in the key.
